title: Lexicographically Smallest Palindromic Permutation Greater Than Target
summary: Given strings s and target of equal length, find the smallest palindromic permutation of s that lexicographically follows target.
statement: Given strings s and target of equal length, find the smallest palindromic permutation of s that lexicographically follows target. If no such permutation exists, return an empty string.
constraints: s and target have the same length up to 300 and contain lowercase letters.
Use every character of s to form a palindrome strictly greater than target.
Return the lexicographically smallest valid palindrome, or empty when none exists.
hints: A palindrome is determined by a permutation of half the character counts plus the unique odd center, if any.
First test an exactly matching half because its mirrored suffix may already exceed target; otherwise find the next greater half permutation.
Backtrack through the matched half, raise the latest possible position minimally, and sort the remaining half.
Half strings order their palindromes lexicographically except for the exact-half suffix case, which is checked explicitly.
editorial: Half strings order their palindromes lexicographically except for the exact-half suffix case, which is checked explicitly.

tests.explanation: The two palindromes are abba and baab; baab is the smallest one above target.
The only palindrome aca is greater than abb.
